qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Regulatory CMC spec-in lock-in across ~75%+ recurring consumables supports pricing power and ~28-30% normalized EBITDA margins.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 5 (Management & Capital Allocation = 0, REJECT). Strong FDA/EMA-validated single-use bioprocessing moat ruined by top-of-cycle debt-funded M&A (€2.4B Polyplus) and subsequent dilutive €1.2B equity raise to pay down debt, reflecting poor capital allocation discipline by parent-controlled management.
qualitative.evidence: Sartorius Stedim Biotech holds an enviable competitive moat in single-use bioprocessing consumables with high regulatory switching costs. However, management severely destroyed shareholder value in 2023 by acquiring Polyplus for €2.4B near the peak of the cell-therapy bubble, pushing leverage to ~4.5x EBITDA. In February 2024, management was forced to execute a dilutive €1.2B capital increase at depressed share prices to pay down parent-company debt, demonstrating egregious capital allocation and disregard for per-share compounding.
